titleEn: Law on the Prevention of and the Fight against the Spread of HIV/AIDS

articles.en: This Law aims to provide for the prevention of, and the fight against, the spread of HIV/AIDS in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

- The State shall promote the implementation of a number of measures as follows:
1. Arrange for knowledge on HIV/AIDS to be integrated into schools.
Such education shall include teaching on the causes, the modes of transmission, the prevention and the consequences of HIV/AIDS as well as of other sexually transmitted diseases, focusing in particular on the ethics of life in accordance with social morality, through integration into the curricula of every level of educational institution, including non-formal education.
2. Arrange seminars and training sessions on the prevention of, and the fight against, the spread of HIV/AIDS for teachers and other instructors assigned to provide further instruction.
3. Arrange for the provision of opinions from communities, associations and organisations in education on HIV and AIDS.

- The State shall arrange for education on HIV and AIDS to be integrated as part of the health services provided through doctors and health officials. The knowledge and capacity of such doctors and health officials shall be further strengthened, including skills for the dissemination of information and education on HIV and AIDS.
1689 The dissemination of education on HIV and AIDS, together with further training, shall be the duty of health care service providers in the private sector so as to contribute to the prevention of, and the fight against, the spread of HIV and AIDS.
Such further training shall include discussion of ethical issues relating to HIV and AIDS, in particular the maintenance of confidentiality and respect for individual rights.

- Arrange for the dissemination of information and for artistic and educational programmes through the State broadcasting networks, free of charge, so that they reach the general public.
Such dissemination shall use appropriate methods and timing so as to ensure effectiveness.
The State shall arrange special education focusing on girls and women who are heads of household, with particular attention to the role of women in society and to gender issues.

- The State shall arrange educational materials for tourists and persons sojourning at international entry and exit points. Such educational materials shall be printed in Khmer and, where necessary, in other languages.
1690

- The State shall arrange to provide information, educational materials or participation in seminars to all Khmer workers, officials of international organisations and civil servants on the causes, the modes of transmission, the prevention and the consequences of HIV/AIDS before they depart to work abroad.

- All ministries, institutions, enterprises and handicraft establishments shall cooperate with the National Authority for Combating AIDS in arranging HIV/AIDS education programmes in the workplace, which shall include topics on the maintenance of confidentiality in the workplace and on the treatment of persons living with HIV and persons with AIDS, together with education on HIV/AIDS. All ministries, institutions, enterprises and handicraft establishments shall prepare plans in accordance with their respective mandates so as to contribute to halting the spread of AIDS.

The State shall mobilise the participation of citizens, families, organisations, the Buddhist clergy, religious orders and groups of persons most at risk in order to arrange the provision of information and education at every level throughout the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Equipment or materials for the prevention of HIV transmission that are supplied by sale or as a gift shall be accompanied by educational materials printed in Khmer and, where necessary, in other languages, which explain the correct method of using such equipment or materials and their effectiveness against HIV transmission.
1691

- All advertising or commercial promotion that makes claims regarding the treatment or the means of preventing HIV/AIDS contrary to the measures of the National Authority for Combating AIDS and to technical medical principles is strictly prohibited.
Chapter 3 Safe Methods and Practices

All methods and practices shall be carried out in accordance with the guidelines of the National Authority for Combating AIDS.
The National Authority for Combating AIDS shall consult and coordinate with the Ministry of Health and the competent entities concerned in order to determine and disseminate guidelines on universal precautions against HIV and AIDS infection, in particular during surgery, dental treatment, tattooing, piercing or other work of a similar nature.
- The use of any blood, tissue or organ shall be preceded by a confirmed HIV test.
_ Laboratories and any other entities are not permitted to collect blood, tissue or organs for use without a prior confirmed HIV test.

..
Relatives or recipients of blood, tissue or organs shall have the right to request a re-test before the transfusion of blood, the grafting of tissue or organ transplantation, except in cases of emergency.
1692

._ Blood, tissue and organs that are infected with HIV shall be destroyed in accordance with the strictest principles of hygiene. Where necessary, blood, tissue or organs infected with HIV may be accepted solely for the purposes of scientific study and research.

- It is strictly prohibited for any person who knows that he or she is infected with HIV/AIDS to engage, with intent, in conduct that transmits it to another person.
Chapter 4 Testing and Counselling

Testing for HIV/AIDS shall be carried out voluntarily and shall require the prior consent of the person concerned. In the case of a minor, the written consent of the legal guardian shall be required.
If the written consent of the legal guardian cannot be obtained, the HIV/AIDS test may be carried out with the mere agreement of the minor, provided that the test offers a direct benefit to that minor.
In the case of a person of unsound mind, the State shall give due attention.

..
It is strictly prohibited to impose a requirement to undergo an HIV/AIDS test prior to or after authorisation to work, admission to study at any educational institution, or for the exercise of the freedom of residence, the right to travel, the provision of medical services or other services.
1693
Compulsory HIV/AIDS testing shall be permitted only in cases where there is an order of a court.

All HIV/AIDS testing shall be carried out anonymously.
The Ministry of Health shall arrange mechanisms for HIV/AIDS testing and shall ensure anonymity and maintain medical confidentiality in the testing process.

- Every HIV testing site may provide this service only if it holds a licence from the Ministry of Health.
The Ministry of Health shall cooperate with the National Authority for Combating AIDS in order to determine and maintain appropriate service standards.

- Every HIV/AIDS testing site shall provide pre-test and post-test counselling to persons who come to request an HIV/AIDS test. Such counsellors shall have adequate capacity in accordance with the standards set by the Ministry of Health.

The National Authority for Combating AIDS and the Ministry of Health shall cooperate in arranging and upgrading the capacity for HIV/AIDS testing at every licensed testing site, and shall ensure the training of specialist personnel to provide such services at the HIV/AIDS testing sites.
1694 Chapter 5 Health Services and Care Services

..
The State shall ensure that persons living with HIV and persons with AIDS receive primary health care free of charge through all State health networks, and shall encourage participation from the private sector.

- The State shall mobilise the participation of citizens, families, organisations, the Buddhist clergy, religious orders and groups of persons most at risk, with a view to supporting, caring for and treating persons living with HIV and persons with AIDS at every level throughout the Kingdom of Cambodia.

- The State shall give attention to promoting vocational training for persons living with HIV and persons with AIDS so as to enable them to earn a living, together with self-help programmes. Persons living with HIV and persons with AIDS shall have the right to participate fully in vocational training programmes and self-help programmes as a means of earning a living.

- The State shall continue to give attention to promoting the prevention of, the fight against and the control of sexually transmitted diseases with a view to contributing to halting the spread of HIV/AIDS.
1695 Chapter 6 Monitoring

The State shall establish a programme for monitoring HIV and AIDS that is broad enough to determine the scale of the risk faced by citizens and their sexual behaviour.
The aim of this programme shall be to verify and evaluate the adequacy, effectiveness and sustainability of the measures for the prevention of, and the fight against, the spread of HIV and AIDS in the country.

Every HIV and AIDS testing site shall adopt measures to ensure the confidentiality of reports, medical records and personal information, including all information that may be obtained from other sources, in the implementation of the monitoring programme. This monitoring programme shall use numerical codes in order to ensure anonymity.

- The tracing of the source of HIV/AIDS transmission and other confidential health research activities may continue to be monitored by the Ministry of Health and the competent institutions concerned, provided that all such activities do not run counter to the general purpose of this Law. The information obtained shall be kept confidential and shall be properly stored.
1696 Chapter 7 Confidentiality

- Persons living with HIV/AIDS shall be entitled to confidentiality.
Medical practitioners, workers, employers, recruitment agencies, insurance companies, data entry operators, keepers of files relating to HIV/AIDS and other persons with related duties shall be instructed to take care to preserve confidentiality in employment relationships, in particular as regards the identity and personal circumstances of persons living with HIV.

- Medical confidentiality shall be waived in the following cases: a. where reporting is required in accordance with the HIV/AIDS monitoring programme as provided in Article 30 of this Law; b. where information is provided to health personnel who are directly or indirectly treating or caring for persons living with HIV/AIDS; and c. where a response is made to an order issued by a court on a matter of importance relating to the HIV/AIDS status of any person. The confidentiality of medical records shall be properly sealed by the records officer after rigorous examination by the responsible official, and they shall be handed over in person and officially opened by the judge before the in camera chamber.
1697

The results of an HIV/AIDS test may be provided to: a. the person who voluntarily requested the HIV/AIDS test; b. the legal guardian of a minor who has been tested for HIV/AIDS; in the case of a person of unsound mind or an orphan, the result shall be provided to the legal guardian; c. persons authorised to receive these results for the HIV/AIDS monitoring programme as provided in Article 30 of this Law; and d. as required by a court, as provided in point c of Article 34 of this Law.

..
It is strictly prohibited to discriminate against any person, in any manner, before or after employment, including in hiring, in promotion, in the assignment of work and in social coexistence, on the sole basis of knowledge or suspicion that that person or that person’s family members are infected with HIV/AIDS. Any dismissal of a person on the basis of knowledge or suspicion that that person or that person’s family members are infected with HIV/AIDS shall be regarded as unlawful.

- No educational or training institution shall refuse admission to, expel, discipline, segregate or deny the benefits of, or any other services to, any pupil or student solely on account of knowledge
1698 or suspicion that that pupil or student, or that pupil’s or student’s family members, are infected with HIV/AIDS.

- Persons living with HIV/AIDS shall have the full right to residence and to travel.
No person shall be confined to a separate place, isolated, denied a shared tenancy, refused travel with others, or expelled on account of knowledge or suspicion that that person or that person’s family members are infected with HIV/AIDS.

- Discrimination against persons living with HIV/AIDS in access to public office is strictly prohibited.
The right to seek public office by election or by appointment to a higher rank shall not be denied to any person solely on account of knowledge or suspicion that that person or that person’s family members are infected with HIV/AIDS.

- Discrimination against persons living with HIV/AIDS in access to all credit and loans is strictly prohibited, including health, accident and life insurance, where the person concerned fulfils the technical conditions in the same manner as an ordinary citizen.

- Discrimination against persons living with HIV/AIDS in hospitals and in all health institutions is strictly prohibited.
1699 No person shall be refused health care services, whether public or private, or be charged a higher price, on account of knowledge that that person or that person’s family members are infected with HIV/AIDS.

- Persons living with HIV/AIDS shall have the same rights as ordinary citizens, as provided in Chapter 3 of the Constitution of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
Chapter 9 National Authority for Combating AIDS (N.A.C.A.)
- The National Authority for Combating AIDS is hereby established in order to lead and implement the work of preventing and fighting the spread of HIV/AIDS in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

- The Prime Minister shall be appointed as the Chairperson of the National Authority for Combating AIDS. In the event that the Prime Minister is unable to perform this function in person, the Prime Minister may appoint a member of the Royal Government to act in his or her place.

The organisation and functioning of the National Authority for Combating AIDS shall be determined by sub-decree.
1700

The State shall include the programme for combating AIDS as a priority activity of the national development programme, and shall promote and facilitate the provision of the annual budget in a timely manner so that this programme achieves its effectiveness.
The budget of the National Authority for Combating AIDS shall be prepared for the ministries concerned and for the provinces and municipalities throughout the Kingdom of Cambodia, and shall be classified as a supplementary budget of the Ministry of Health and included under the priority budget chapter.

In order to ensure the effectiveness of the multi-sectoral response, the National Authority for Combating AIDS shall receive support in mobilising resources, both domestic and external, and in coordinating and directing the use of those resources to the institutions concerned, in accordance with the actual situation and needs of the national strategic plan programme.
Chapter 10 Penal Provisions

- Any person who commits an act contrary to Article 12 of this Law shall be liable to a fine of from 500,000 (five hundred thousand) riels to 1,000,000 (one million) riels and to imprisonment of from 1 (one) month to 1 (one) year.
In the case of recidivism, the penalty shall be doubled. Civil servants shall additionally be subject to administrative sanctions.
1701

- Any person who commits an act contrary to Article 13, Article 14 or Article 15 of this Law shall be liable to a fine of from
500,000 (five hundred thousand) riels to 1,000,000 (one million) riels and to imprisonment of from
6 (six) months to 1 (one) year. In the case of recidivism, the penalty shall be doubled. This penalty shall not preclude liability for civil compensation and the withdrawal of the professional licences concerned. Civil servants shall additionally be subject to administrative sanctions.

Any person who commits an act contrary to Article 18 of this Law shall be liable to imprisonment of from 10 (ten) years to
15 (fifteen) years.

Any person who commits an offence contrary to Article 30, Article 31 or Article 32 of this Law shall be liable to a fine of from
50,000 (fifty thousand) riels to 200,000 (two hundred thousand) riels and to imprisonment of from 1 (one) month to 6 (six) months. In the case of recidivism, the penalty shall be doubled. Civil servants shall additionally be subject to administrative sanctions.

- Any person who commits an act contrary to Article 36, Article 37, Article 38, Article 39, Article 40 or Article 41 of this Law shall be liable to a fine of from 100,000 (one hundred thousand) riels to 1,000,000 (one million) riels and to imprisonment of from 1 (one) month to 6 (six) months. In the case of recidivism, the penalty shall be doubled.
Civil servants shall additionally be subject to administrative sanctions.
1702 Chapter 11 Final Provisions Article 53.- Any provision contrary to this Law shall be considered null and void.
